text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed 11% over the past week, with today's modest gain (+0.44%) continuing a strong recovery from an early-November dip. The rally tracks a broader refining environment where crude prices have stabilized in the $89–$92 range, refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year—a shift that typically boosts refiner margins since they profit from the spread between crude input costs and refined product prices.

However, the longer picture shows a headwind: Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day, pushing global oil markets back into surplus according to the International Energy Agency. More supply in the world market can pressure the price spreads refiners rely on, which may explain why the stock is still down 6.76% over two weeks despite this week's bounce.
